title: Take the collar off the dog manikin
instruction: Take the collar off the dog manikin: unclip the buckle, draw the collar off its neck, lay it on the table beside the manikin and let go of it.
context: Taking the collar off for the night is a routine act for dog owners; about 65 million US households keep a dog (APPA 2023-24). Most collars close with a plastic side-release buckle: two sprung prongs on the male half hook behind ribs inside the female and let go only while both side tabs are pressed in at once, thumb and finger of one hand, while the other hand pulls the male out. Pulling the male alone drags the whole collar round the neck; pressing the tabs and then letting go to pull lets both hooks catch again, so the pinch must be held through the whole pull. A collar fitted with the usual two-finger room will not pass over the dog's head, so once open it is drawn round and out from under the neck and put down. The skill is a one-hand pinch on a 29 mm part right beside the other hand drawing its mate out, then pulling a loose strap out from under a body without catching it.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top; arm bases at y +305 and -305. Nothing is clamped. Figures marked est are the task's design values (the sim is built to them), not maker data. (1) Dog manikin: a Simulaids CasPeR CPR dog manikin, item 100-5000 (about US$460 from medical-training suppliers; 711 x 584 x 254 mm, 6.8 kg, per the retailer), loose on its right side, head toward the robot, back toward -y, legs toward +y, nose tip on a tape mark at (88, 8), rump on a tape mark at x 800. A lower-cost stand-in is any firm life-size lying-dog figure (for example a Douglas Sadie yellow Lab plush, about 760 mm long, about US$130) laid on its right side that passes the checks below; a figure under 5 kg has sandbags laid on its upper flank between x 450 and 750, clear of the neck and head, to bring it to 5 to 9 kg. Neck (est): along x from 265 to 380, 104 mm across, 327 mm round, top 129 mm up, underside 25 mm above the table (head and chest carry it). Behind the ears the head is 132 mm across, 415 mm round (est): more than the collar's loop, so the buckled collar cannot come off over the head. (2) Collar, worn: a Blueberry Pet Classic nylon dog collar, size M, 3/4 in (19 mm) red webbing, 33 g (est), 381 mm round its middle, in the plane x 320 round the neck, its slack hanging under the neck. Its black plastic 3/4 in side-release buckle (56 x 29 x 11 mm closed, est; the sim draws the female dark grey so the seam shows) lies on top of the neck, long axis along y: female housing from y -4 to +30, mouth toward -y, 29 mm wide; male toward -y, 22 mm of it showing (y -26 to -4), 25 mm wide, its back the webbing bar. The male has a centre tongue and two sprung side prongs; each prong's press tab shows through a slot in a side of the female, open from the mouth, centred 14 mm in from the mouth, and stands 1.5 mm proud; its hook sits behind a 1.3 mm rib inside the female (est). A tab pressed flush takes 2.5 N (est); a hook clears its rib once its tab is about 0.9 mm in. The male slides out only while both tabs are held in. A pen line on the male marks the female's mouth when clicked. A steel D-ring (25 x 20 mm, est) lies flat on the webbing next to the male, on the neck's -y side; the black tri-glide is on the neck's +y side. Nothing else is on the table. Checks before the first trial (ruler, calipers, 0-10 N spring scale, kitchen scale); use the parts only if all pass, and any 3/4 in side-release collar that passes may stand in: buckle 56 x 29 x 11 mm, each within 2 mm; each tab pressed flush by 1.5 to 4 N; loop 381 mm round, within 10 mm; collar 10 to 40 g; manikin 5 to 9 kg with any sandbags; neck 327 mm round, within 30 mm, with a 25 mm block passing under it (if it does not, set the head and the shoulder on two 20 to 25 mm rubber pads outside the collar's path, one under the head at x under 250, one under the chest at x over 400, and check again); head behind the ears at least 30 mm more round than the loop, and the buckled collar does not pass over it when drawn toward the nose by hand.
scoring: Sim reads the poses of the buckle halves, the webbing links (with the D-ring and tri-glide), the manikin and the grippers; the real trial reads the trial video, an end photo, a ruler and blocks. Each rule names both. The two latches count from the first step to the last; other states are read at the last step unless a rule says otherwise. Latch A, collar off the table: any part of the collar more than 3 mm below the table top or past its edge on any step (real: the video). Latch B, manikin dragged: its nose tip or rump 100 mm or more from where it started on any step. Nudged: either 20 mm or more from where it started on any step; this only caps the score (sim: those two points on the manikin's pose; real: distance from its tape mark, ruler on the end photo or any frame). Unlatched: the male's pen line 3 mm or more out of the mouth (sim: the male's slide along the female's axis). Apart: every part of the male 5 mm or more outside the female's outer box (real: no part of the male in the mouth, its prong tips 5 mm or more out, ruler on the end photo). Off the manikin: every part of the collar (webbing, both buckle halves, D-ring, tri-glide) 25 mm or more from the manikin (sim: distance to its collision shapes; real: a 25 mm block passes between collar and manikin along the whole collar without moving either). Resting: no part of the collar more than 40 mm above the table top and no part moving 5 mm/s or faster (real: ruler; no part moves 5 mm or more in the last 1 s of video). Hands off: both grippers' finger zones 30 mm or more from every part of the collar (real: no finger touches the collar in the last 1 s of video, and a 30 mm block passes between each gripper's fingers and the collar with the arms held in their last pose). Score 0 if either latch fired. Otherwise: 1.0 if apart, off the manikin, resting and hands off all hold on every step of the last 1 s (20 steps; real: the last 1 s of video and the end checks) and the manikin was never nudged; 0.75 if apart and off the manikin at the last step but resting or hands off fails on a step of the last 1 s (collar still held, touched, moving or raised) or the manikin was nudged; 0.5 if apart at the last step but some part of the collar within 25 mm of the manikin (still round or under the neck); 0.25 if unlatched but not apart; 0 if the pen line is less than 3 mm out (still buckled). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0; every end state falls in exactly one. The score does not read the tabs or the order of moves: a male pulled without both tabs held in stays caught by its hooks, and the head stops the buckled collar from coming off over it.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The manikin: one loose 6.8 kg body of cylinders and boxes to the maker's outline. Buckle: the female housing with its two catch ribs; the male a separate body with two prongs on vertical hinges with springs (2.5 N at the tab, flush), hooks catching the ribs: contact only, no rule. Webbing: 13 rigid 25 x 19 x 2 mm links on hinges whose axes run along the neck, so it bends but does not twist or stretch; it is glued to the male's bar. D-ring and tri-glide ride on links.
reset_notes: Pass the collar under the manikin's neck, bring both ends up over the top and push the male into the female until both tabs click: buckle on top of the neck, female toward +y, D-ring beside the male, the male's pen line at the female's mouth, the collar's plane at x 320. Put the manikin's nose and rump back on their tape marks. The checks in setup are done once per new collar or manikin, not every trial.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (one arm idle: 0.0 left idle, 0.0 right idle)
